n: A king will reign with righteousness and his officials will govern with justice. This may first describe a good king like Hezekiah, but it reaches its fullness in the Messiah’s reign.

f.w: a king shall reign in righteousness

n: Each such leader will be like a shelter from wind and storm, streams in the desert, and the shade of a great rock in a weary land. True leaders protect and refresh.

f.w: an hiding place from the wind
the shadow of a great rock

n: Then eyes will no longer be closed and ears will listen — reversing the spiritual blindness of Isaiah 6.

f.w: the eyes of them that see shall not be dim

n: The hasty will gain understanding, and those who stammered will speak clearly.
Fools will no longer be called noble, and scoundrels will no longer be respected. Society will see people as they truly are.
For the fool speaks foolishness and plots evil, acts godlessly, spreads error about the Lord, and leaves the hungry empty and the thirsty without drink.

f.w: make empty the soul of the hungry

n: The scoundrel’s methods are evil; he schemes to ruin the poor with lies, even when the needy person’s cause is just.
But the noble person plans noble things, and by generous deeds he stands firm.
Isaiah calls on the complacent, carefree women of Jerusalem to wake up and listen.
In a little over a year, you careless ones will tremble, because the grape harvest will fail and the fruit won’t come in.

f.g: Literally “days upon a year” — in a little more than a year.

n: Tremble and shudder! Strip off your fine clothes and wear sackcloth in mourning.
They will beat their breasts in grief for the pleasant fields and fruitful vines that are lost.
Thorns and briers will cover the land of God’s people, even the happy homes of the once-joyful city.
The palace will be deserted, the busy city abandoned, and its forts and watchtowers will become dens for wild donkeys and pastures for flocks.

f.g: Possibly “Ophel and watchtower” — Ophel was a hill in Jerusalem.

n: This will last until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high. Then the wilderness will become fertile and the fertile field like a forest — spiritual renewal transforms everything.

f.w: the spirit be poured upon us from on high
the wilderness be a fruitful field

n: Justice will dwell in the wilderness and righteousness in the fruitful field.
The fruit of righteousness will be peace, and its result quietness and confidence forever. Peace grows from righteous living.

f.w: the work of righteousness shall be peace

n: God’s people will live in peaceful homes, secure dwellings, and undisturbed resting places.
Even if hail flattens the forest and the city is laid low, God’s people will be safe. The proud “forest” and “city” of the world will fall.
Blessed are you who sow by every stream and let your ox and donkey roam freely — a picture of peaceful, abundant life.
